Between:
Chukka Ravikanth and Others ...PETITIONER/ACCUSED(S)
 AND The State Of Andhra Pradesh and ...RESPONDENT/COMPLAINANT(S)

1.
CH MURALI KRISHNA Counsel for the Respondent/complainant(S):
1. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR (AP)

The Court made the following Order:-
This Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioners/A3 and A4, under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, seeking to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.732 of 2017 on the file of III Metropolitan Magistrate, Vishakhapatnam for the offence punishable under Sections 420 IPC & Section 76 r/w 3, 4 of Chit Fund Act, 1982.
2. Heard Sri Ch.Murali Krishna, learned counsel for the petitioners.
Learned counsel for the petitioners filed an affidavit to the effect that the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor before the trial court refused to take the notice though ordered by this court.

Heard Ms. K. Priyanka Lakshmi,
learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for the respondents.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the petitioners herein are the children of Accused Nos. 1 and 2.

Accused No.3 is the son and Accused No.4 is the daughter of the Accused Nos.
1 and 2.

Learned counsel would further submit that except making bald statement that Accused Nos.
1 and 2 purchased properties in the name of Accused Nos. 3 and 4 and preserved the gold in bank,

1 nothing is there against them to attract the offence punishable under Sections 420 IPC & Section 76 r/w 3, 4 of Chit Fund Act, 1982.

sentences.text: Learned counsel would further submit that the alleged cheating said to have been taken place prior to 15.10.2015, by that time, the petitioners i.e., Accused Nos. 3 and 4 were minors.
They have nothing to do with the alleged case against their parents.
Learned counsel would submit that Accused Nos. 1 and 2 filed insolvency petition and that was allowed.
The names of the petitioners are not there in the complaint but they were in the charge sheet.
Learned counsel finally submits that continuing criminal proceedings against the petitioners is mere abuse of process of law.

4. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submit that it is alleged against the petitioners that Accused Nos. 1 and 2 have purchased property in the name of Accused Nos. 3 and 4 and preserved some gold in the bank.

Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor fairly conceded that no iota of evidence is placed even in the charge sheet to show that any property purchased in the name of Accused Nos.
3 and 4 by Accused Nos. 1 and 2, after they became majors.
Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor finally submits that court may pass appropriate orders taking into consideration the facts and circumstances.

5. Considering the submissions made and a fair look at the contents of the statement of the respondent No.2 basing on which the crime is registered would show that Accused Nos. 1 and 2 have been doing chit fund business apart from provisions shop for 10 years preceding to the lodging of the complaint.
The complaint further would show that Accused Nos. 1 and 2 started the business chit fund from 2005.
As can be seen from the charge sheet, the age of Accused No.3 was shown as 23 years and Accused No.4 as 20 years respectively.

As rightly put by the learned counsel for the petitioner, even if any property alleged to have been purchased by Accused Nos. 1 and 2 in the name of the Accused Nos. 3 and 4, they were minors, and they have nothing to do with the alleged case against their parents.

Furthermore, as rightly put by the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor, there is no reference in the charge sheet about any information collected during the course of investigation to buttress the contentions of the complainant that Accused Nos. 1 and 2 purchased properties in the name of their children or any gold is preserved in the bank in the name of Accused Nos. 3 and 4.
Needless to say that there is no concept of vicarious liability in criminal case unless their role is specifically alleged under Section 34 or under Section 149 or by any statute.
In the present case, it appears only to rope the family members of the Accused Nos. 1 and 2 as an arm twist, the case is lodged against their children.
In that view, continuing criminal proceedings against the petitioners i.e., Accused Nos. 3 and 4 is mere abuse of process of law.
6. In the result, the petition is allowed.

C.C.No.732 of 2017 on the file of III Metropolitan Magistrate,
Vishakhapatnam for theoffence punishable under Sections 420 IPC & Section 76 r/w 3, 4 of Chit Fund Act, 1982 qua the petitioners/Accused Nos. 3 and 4 is hereby quashed.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
